A2 is gone from the store, from history (loadProject clears past/future), and was never PUT — unrecoverable, the exact loss class S79-B closed for the machine-idle case (the e2e probe pins only that case: "add 3 circles … pushState-swap inside the window" fires with flushing === false). Fix shape: capture the newer state at the boundary even while flushing (a captured-body cleanup PUT like the unmount path's), or have the swap guard re-arm via a live-refs compare before dropping.
- [Low] S79-A residual — an Untitled→Untitled LOAD (a lineage break with the ""→"" projectId shape) keeps the stale transcript and renders a silently no-op Revert. ai-assistant.tsx:121 — `if (state.projectId === prevState.projectId) return;` fires before the epoch check, so a soft swap /Editor?projectId=unknown1 → /Editor?projectId=unknown2 (both fall to the Untitled fallback, editor-view.tsx:1289-1292) replaces the canvas (boardEpoch moves, elements wiped) while the old conversation survives; a surviving carrier's Revert button still renders (ai-assistant.tsx:475, keyed on revertSnapshot presence only) but the epoch belt (ai-assistant.tsx:271) makes the click a silent no-op — the "a control that lies about its state" / S76-C "a control that cannot work must not render" class. - [Low] AI apply: one LLM update op carrying BOTH scale and a paint/geometry patch pushes TWO undo history entries. ai-assistant.tsx:217-223 — `store.scaleElements(targets, ...)` then `store.updateElements(targets, patch)` (default commit=true); scaleElements (editor-store.ts:316-321) and updateElements (editor-store.ts:294-295) each push a `past` snapshot, so "make it red and 25% bigger" costs two Ctrl+Z presses with a visible intermediate state — the one-entry-per-intent doctrine (S56-A/S62-A) violated for this interleaving (the honest count correctly reads ONE; the pre-apply Revert snapshot covers full recovery, so impact is undo granularity only).

Findings:
- MEDIUM — editor-view.tsx:507-513 — the machine-carries skip branch records NO leave-transport: when the user exits while the machine's own PUT₁ is in flight with no newer edit (machineCarriesThisState true — exit()-inside-the-800ms-save window), the cleanup skips its PUT₂ AND leaves leaveTransportFor null, so a same-project re-entry mount's GET awaits NOTHING and can answer BEFORE PUT₁ lands (slow PUT: a large board's full-list replace, a slow uplink). loadProject then replaces the store's still-correct element list with the pre-edit server state and stamps it "saved"; the disposed machine drops PUT₁'s healing response; the next local edit's full-list PUT permanently deletes the pre-exit edit server-side — the exact S85-A GET/PUT race, surviving in the one branch the registry never covered. Fix: in the skip branch register `leaveTransportFor = { projectId: state.projectId, done: softLeaveDescriptor.flightDone }` (the machine's surviving flight IS the transport; the registry's done already accepts a bare promise). Secondary edge of the same hole: the single-slot one-shot drain means an intervening OTHER-project mount consumes the slot without awaiting, so a same-project re-entry through a third project also loses the await.
- LOW — canvas.tsx:295-304/:317-323 + editor-store.ts:339-355 — the canvas gesture family (draw commit, moveElements' accumulated dx/dy, the resize write-back) writes x/y/width/height with NO bound: the last unclamped consumers of the server's clampNumber(±100000 / 0..100000) row-builder bounds. An element dragged (or drawn after panning) past ±100000 canvas units (reachable in ~5-10 max-zoom-out drags: 2000px screen at zoom 0.1 = 20000 units each) renders locally, then visibly teleports to the clamped bound when the store-replacing PUT lands — the S84-B/S86-B teleport family's canvas member. Fix: route the draw commit + resize write-back through clampPositionField/clampSizeField, and clamp the accumulated position in moveElements.
- LOW — properties-panel.tsx:139-148 (NumberField) and :231-238 (GuardedNumberInput) — the blur restore fires only for EMPTY/unparseable drafts; a PARSEABLE-but-clamped draft never resyncs when the consumer clamp maps it back to the field's CURRENT value (type 500000 into an X field already at 100000 → clampPositionField returns 100000 → the external value never changes → the render-time compare never fires → the field displays 500000 indefinitely while the model/canvas/server hold 100000; same at rotation/opacity/W/H bounds). HexColorRow's S79-E blur-restore (`setDraft(value ?? "")`) already closes the color twin; the numeric family lacks the same restore. Fix: on blur, resync the draft from the committed model value whenever `Number(draft) !== value` (not only when unparseable).

B146-M1 (Medium — the session's LIVE finding, classified TEST-SIDE): tests/e2e/session77-fixes.spec.ts:30 — the fixed `waitForTimeout(1000)` racing the cross-process context-page creation after `link.click({ modifiers: ["Control"] })` (:29), with the unbounded-outcome assertion `expect(pages.length).toBeGreaterThan(pagesBefore)` (:33) reading `context().pages()` at the sleep's fixed end. Evidence: the baseline full-suite gate failed this test 2 of 3 runs (261/262; "Expected > 1, Received 1" — the new tab never registered within 1000ms) while passing 4/4 in isolation; the config is workers:1 / fullyParallel:false (playwright.config.ts:34-35), so the differential is cumulative-load latency (one shared Chromium process + standalone server ~7 minutes into the run), never cross-test interference; the app-side seam is verified correct (recent-view.tsx:196-198 returns early on meta/ctrl/shift/alt — the native anchor behavior preserved, no preventDefault on the modifier path). Impact: a reproducible false-red on the delivery gate — rerun cost + alarm fatigue on a green build; zero product surface. Recommended fix: replace the sleep + count read with a bounded poll on the URL predicate — `await expect.poll(() => page.context().pages().some((p) => p.url().includes("/Editor?projectId=")), { timeout: 10_000 }).toBe(true)` — NOT a count-only poll: the count increments when the page object exists while its URL can still be about:blank (the navigation commits after creation), so the robust form polls the discriminator itself (the /Editor?projectId= URL), which subsumes both the creation and the navigation; `page.context().waitForEvent("page")` is the equivalent event-driven alternative (the CONTEXT-level "page" event fires for no-opener tabs — only the PAGE-level "popup" event requires the opener relationship, the distinction the spec's own :23-27 comment records). Confidence: high (mechanism deterministic-cause; isolation-vs-suite differential + serial config + verified app seam).

B146-L1 (Low — the same defect class, unfailed sibling): tests/e2e/autosave-race.spec.ts:105 — the fixed `waitForTimeout(2_500)` racing the fire-and-forget EXIT-FLUSH PUT's server-side commit before the reopen's GET reads the board state (:106-113 assert the background persisted). The raced outcome is a NETWORK SETTLE: the exit flush rides the spec's own 700ms route-injected delay (:89-92 — a delay that itself executes in the loaded test process and stretches under load) plus the full-replace transaction; 2500ms ≈ 3.5x the injected delay, the margin that has kept it green historically, but the S77-B datum (a 1000ms bound failing at 2-of-3 under the same full-suite load) shows the class is live on this machine. On a slow crossing the reopen GET reads pre-commit state and `toHaveValue("#1a2b3c")` false-fails a good build. Recommended fix: capture the response promise BEFORE the Back click — `const flushDone = page.waitForResponse((r) => r.request().method() === "PUT" && r.url().includes("/elements"));` — then `await flushDone` after the Dashboard URL settles and before reopening. Confidence: high on the structural class, medium on the flake likelihood (no observed failure).

B146-I1 (Informational — the coverage-degrade members, zero good-build flake): the two UNHARDENED orchestration sleeps — tests/e2e/autosave-race.spec.ts:55 and tests/e2e/session60-fixes.spec.ts:137, both `waitForTimeout(1_000)` "past the 800ms debounce so flush A is in flight" before edit B lands. Evidence: charAt is UTF-16 code-unit-based — a name whose first character is an astral-plane character (an emoji, e.g. "😀 Designer") yields the LONE HIGH SURROGATE, which React renders as a broken-glyph/tofu character in the chip; the "D"/"M" fallback never fires because the lone-surrogate string is TRUTHY (the S77-D family closed the whitespace-leading blank-chip member; the astral member is a different axis of the same first-character seam). tests/user-initial.test.ts pins the trim/upper/fallback FORM, not the code-point form. Impact: cosmetic-only, edge-case (astral-first display names), zero data/security surface, both the header chip and every card's first avatar affected on such names. Recommended fix: the code-point-aware form at the family's sites — `[...user.name.trim()][0]?.toUpperCase() || "D"` (spread iterates code points; the optional chain keeps the empty-name fallback) — or one shared `initialFor(name, fallback)` seam the five sites consume (the F35e single-source rule). Confidence: Reasoned (JavaScript string semantics verified; no live render executed this audit).

A146-L2 (Low — the F88 form-alignment family's render-surface residual, the thumbnail's overflow divergence): project-card.tsx:194 — CanvasThumbnail's element div carries `overflow: "hidden"` UNCONDITIONALLY, while both siblings gate it text-only: canvas.tsx:991 (`style.overflow = "hidden"` set only inside `if (element.type === "text")`) and the PresentOverlay at editor-view.tsx:1155 (`overflow: el.type === "text" ? "hidden" : undefined`). Evidence: a line element's SVG diagonal is absolutely positioned inside the element div (`absolute left-0 top-0 overflow-visible`), and the transformed/positioned parent is its containing block, so `overflow: hidden` clips the stroke to the element's box — a freshly drawn LINE (defaultGeometry: `height: 0`, strokeWidth 2) renders a 0-height clipped box in every Dashboard/Recent card thumbnail (the line INVISIBLE in the card while fully rendered in the editor/present/export), and a thick-stroke diagonal loses its strokeLinecap round caps at the box edge in thumbnails only. The seed carries no line (prisma/seed.ts: frame/rectangle/ellipse/text only), so the seeded demo does not exhibit it — but the Line tool is one of nine, and any user-drawn horizontal/vertical line hits the invisible case. Impact: cosmetic divergence confined to the 320x200 list thumbnails; the canvas/present/SVG-export renders agree with each other; zero data surface (the model is untouched). Recommended fix: align the thumbnail to the family form — `overflow: el.type === "text" ? "hidden" : undefined` (the canvas sibling's exact ternary); a e2e/unit pin on the thumbnail line form would close the F88 membership honestly. Confidence: Reasoned (CSS containing-block + clipping semantics are deterministic; no live render executed this audit).

### I-1 (Informational — UX edge, the S184-A documented tradeoff's residual)
- **Location**: src/components/login-screen.tsx:246–255.
- **Description**: the autofill-distribution branch fires for ANY multi-char value at index 0 — including a manual append into a FILLED first cell (click filled cell 0, type one digit → value "35" → code distributes as 3,5 and **wipes cells 2–5**). - **Impact**: rare manual-edit path loses digits 3–6 of a partially-entered code; self-heals on retype/paste/autofill.
- **Fix** (optional): discriminate "value length > 6 or equals a fresh autofill" vs "length 2 at a filled cell", or accept and register the residual in the S184-A comment.
